newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FOCUS - TAM deal boosts overseas plans.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - TAM deal boosts overseas plans.

text.p: The sale of a minority stake in airline group TAM for 80 million ($75 million) will allow Brazil's top regional carrier to offer overseas flights, a company official said.

TAM board President Antonio Luiz Teixeira de Barros told Reuters that the company, Brazil's fastest-growing air carrier, received authorization to set daily flights to Miami and is planning flights to Europe.
The sale of a 22.86-percent stake in the firm, announced late Thursday, will enable TAM to "consolidate its international operations without compromising its cash-flow," Barros said.
The TAM group expects to complete in two months an on-going reorganization to allow the expansion, including the merger of all its five operating units into a new holding company, he said.
Barros added that TAM will sign an agreement with American Airlines on April 29 but declined to say what kind of an accord would be signed.
TAM, already operating abroad through its recently purchased Paraguayan unit Transportes Aereos do Mercosul, will begin flying to Miami sometime between November and April 1998, Barros said.
It also plans to lease at least two Boeing or Airbus aircraft for its new overseas flights, he said.

"We're planning to lease two Boeing 767-300 or Airbus 330-200 with an option to lease another three (aircraft)," he said, adding that market studies to decide which planes to lease will be completed in 60 days.

To enable the expansion, the airline's owner Rolim Adolfo Amaro raised the money by selling a 22.86-percent stake, comprised of preferred shares, in the group's operations to four private equity funds managed by Banco Garantia and BEA Capital.
A TAM statement sent to the Sao Paulo bourse Thursday identified the funds as Brazil Private Equity S.A., Brazilian Equity Ltd, Brazilian Equity Investments and Latin America Capital.
Reports of the capital injection at TAM sent its preferred shares soaring 9.6 percent in early trade.
The deal gives new impetus to a company that already has grown at an astounding rate in recent years despite a tragic accident in Sao Paulo that claimed 98 lives in October.

Since 1994, sales at TAM have jumped 74 percent to an estimated $650 million this year from $374 million while the number of passangers has surged 186 percent to a projected 4.7 million this year from 1.6 million three years ago.
Currently, TAM's fleet is comprised of 30 Fokker 100s, nine Fokker F-50s, 38 Caravans as well as 22 small craft and helicopters.
